seats: secular academic scholar of the Bible

fixes.row: Sacrifice in days to come: offered again, or brought to an end
readers: secular academic scholar of the Bible
fixes.why: 'Brought to an end' fits Dan 9:27 only. Hos 3:4 describes Israel's long season without sacrifice, pillar, ephod or idol, in a passage that goes on to return; it does not say sacrifice is ended. Ps 51:19 is a prayer for Zion's rebuilding ('then'), not a statement about days to come. The heading reads a fulfilled-and-ended frame (Heb 10:18) back onto Hosea and Daniel.
fixes.fix: Relabel to 'Sacrifice in days to come: offered, or absent'. In the note say Hos 3:4 is 'many days without sacrifice' for Israel, and Ps 51:19 follows a prayer for Zion's walls; keep the Dan 9:27 'who is he' sentence.

fixes.row: The Lord's table: blood "poured out", "in remembrance of Me", "a participation"
readers: secular academic scholar of the Bible
fixes.why: Only 1 Cor 10:18 has a sacrifice word; Luke 22:19 has neither sacrifice nor blood. The note's reason ('the card ties the Last Supper to sacrifice') is the site's own claim and reads as if the text made it. For the story's arc, the earlier verse Exod 24:8 'the blood of the covenant', beside Exod 24:5's burnt and peace offerings, is not shown, so Matt 26:28 appears with no root.
fixes.fix: Rephrase the note to say these verses are here because they speak of blood, covenant and the meal, and that only 1 Cor 10:18 names a sacrifice; do not attribute the tie to 'the card'. Add a pointer to Exod 24:5-8 ('the blood of the covenant', with the burnt and peace offerings of 24:5). Keep 'the page takes no side'.

fixes.row: Offered again and again, unable to cleanse; once for all
readers: secular academic scholar of the Bible
fixes.why: The label states in the page's voice that the law's sacrifices are 'unable to cleanse'. That is Hebrews' argument, not the account of the Torah texts (which say the priest 'will make atonement ... he will be forgiven', Lev 4:26). A reader of the label alone takes it as the text's whole account.
fixes.fix: Relabel 'Hebrews: offered again and again, unable to cleanse; once for all'. Optionally add to the note that the Torah rows above say what the sacrifices were given to do.

fixes.row: Every other use: sacrificed, offered (verb catch-all)
fixes.why: Two of the four examples shown first, Mark 14:12 (Passover) and Jas 2:21 (Isaac), belong to the named Passover and Isaac rows, so 'every other use' opens on verses that are not other. The note's own list (Heb 5:7, John 16:2, 2 Sam 6:13, 1 Kgs 8:5) is the real content.
fixes.fix: Choose the four examples from the note's list (Heb 5:7, John 16:2, 2 Sam 6:13, 1 Kgs 8:5); correct the note's 'Abraham offering Isaac (Heb 11:17; Jas 2:21)', since those two sit in the Isaac row.

fixes.row: A son or daughter given in sacrifice
readers: secular academic scholar of the Bible
fixes.why: Jephthah's vow (Judg 11:31, 39) is the one place Israel's story puts a child under a burnt-offering promise, with no judgment in the verse; it sits unnoticed in the catch-all. The note also says Hos 13:2 is 'in the row for other gods' without saying which form.
fixes.fix: Name Judg 11:31 in this row's note (the vow 'I will offer it up as a burnt offering', the verse saying nothing of approval) or move it in; say 'the verb row for other gods' for Hos 13:2.

fixes.row: Sacrifice and sin: the sin offering, the guilt offering, "for sins"
fixes.why: This row and 'Atonement made; a hand laid on the head' share Lev 4 and overlap heavily (Lev 4:24 is an example of both), so a reader sees one subject cut in two.
fixes.fix: Keep both, but each note should say 'see the row above/below' for the Lev 4-5 sin-offering ritual, or merge if the row count is needed. No change of verses.

worker_points.point: 1. What a sacrifice does (aroma, atonement, blood, eating, sin) with no side taken
worker_points.why: The atonement note quotes Lev 4:26 and 5:10 as the text has them; 'he will be forgiven' is the Berean's rendering and is not a penal reading. Rows run in the Bible's order, so none is ranked.
Row 15's label ('brought to an end') and row 17's label carry the 'ended' frame in the page's voice; see fixes. Row 11's label itself is neutral and its note sets the readings side by side.
Correct: the Hebrew has no 'merely'. Saying so in the note is true to the original and keeps both readings open. Record it as a translation finding as the worker suggests.

worker_points.point: 4. Lord's Supper row: widen, keep or drop
worker_points.why: Keep, but re-explain it and point back to Exod 24:5-8 (see fixes). Do not widen with Mark 14:22-24, Matt 26:26-27 or Heb 13:10, which carry no sacrifice word.
The note separates verses that name Christ (Heb 9:14, 9:28, 1 Cor 5:7) from those inside Hebrews' argument ('He', 'Himself'); the label asserts only what 1 Cor 5:7 and Heb 9:14, 9:28 say.

worker_points.point: 6. Eating from the sacrifice as communion
worker_points.why: Lev 7:15, Deut 12:27 and 1 Cor 10:18 are shown as they read; Ezek 39:17-19 and Hos 9:4 kept as hard verses; three readings listed with no ranking.
Placed with 10:12 and 10:18 and the note takes no side on falling away.
Gen 22:13 'in place of his son' is the text's own phrase; test, substitute and picture are listed as readings, none favoured.
Hard verses are kept (good); add Jephthah's vow in the note, see fixes.

worker_points.point: 10. Other gods: Paul on food sacrificed to idols beside Naaman's vow
worker_points.why: The row labels itself 'beside another god', and the verses show it; no resolution of 1 Cor 8-10 is offered.
Kept in the blood and eating rows and named; Isa 34:6, Jer 46:10 and Ezek 39:17-19 read as the text has them.
None placed by rule; 'to the LORD' and 'Christ offered Himself' say what the verses say.

missing.what: The covenant ratified with burnt and peace offerings and 'the blood of the covenant', the root of Matt 26:28 (Exod 24:8 has no sacrifice word; 24:5 is in the hub)
Dedication of the altar, tabernacle and temple by sacrifice, a clear step in the story now unmarked in the catch-all
Jephthah's vow, the child under a burnt-offering promise, sits only in the catch-all

examples_checked: 23 of 24 rows' examples show their label; the verb catch-all opens on two verses that belong to named rows (Mark 14:12, Jas 2:21), see fixes. Gen 22:7 and Exod 23:18 recur as examples under two rows each, which is acceptable.
summary: The hub keeps close to the text, sets the readings side by side with no ranking, and keeps the hard verses (child sacrifice, the LORD's sacrificial feast, Jer 7:22). Three labels or notes put a later frame into earlier texts (days-to-come 'brought to an end', Hebrews 'unable to cleanse', the Supper tie), and the arc lacks its root in Exod 24 and the dedications.
